content.title: Why Isn’t ‘The Bachelorette’ on Tonight? The Real Reason Taylor Frankie Paul’s Season Was Pulled
content.text: Key PointsABC pulled The Bachelorette after a disturbing 2023 video of Taylor Frankie Paul surfaced.The video shows a violent altercation involving Taylor, her boyfriend, and her daughter.The season may still air later, with decisions pending due to financial and ownership factors. If you tuned in Sunday night expecting the premiere of Taylor Frankie Paul’s season of The Bachelorette, you’re not alone. The show was originally scheduled to debut on Sunday, March 22—but at the last minute, ABC pulled the season from its schedule. So what happened? Related: ‘Bachelorette’ May Not Be Dead Yet—Insiders Say Taylor Frankie Paul’s Season Could Still Air ABC made the decision to pull season 22 after a 2023 video involving Taylor and her then-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen surfaced publicly on TMZ. In a statement to Parade, the network said, “In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family.” The move came just days before the planned premiere, after ABC had previously indicated earlier in the week that the show was still moving forward. Related: Why Was Taylor Frankie Paul Arrested? Inside the ‘Bachelorette’ Star’s 2023 Assault Case YesYes48%NoNo52% What Happened in the Video? The video shows a 2023 altercation between Taylor and Dakota where she is yelling, throwing chairs and trying to kick Dakota. Her daughter Indy is present in the video, starting to cry as the situation escalates. Indy was reportedly struck accidentally during the incident Taylor later plead guilty to aggravated assault. The resurfacing of that footage prompted ABC’s abrupt decision to pull the season. Related: How Many Kids Does Taylor Frankie Paul Have? Meet the ‘Bachelorette’ Star’s 3 Children Will ‘The Bachelorette’ Still Air? Even though the show has been pulled, it may not be gone for good. According to Variety, ABC could lose tens of millions of dollars if the season never airs, including licensing fees, marketing costs and lost advertising revenue. There’s also a key complication: ABC doesn’t actually own The Bachelorette. The series is produced by Warner Bros. Television Group, which distributes it internationally. That means the studio still has a financial incentive to find a way for the season to be released. Insiders told Variety that Warner Bros. is currently taking a “wait-and-see” approach, staying in contact with ABC as the situation develops. Related: What Is ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’? Inside the MomTok Swinging Scandal That Made Taylor Frankie Paul Famous Possible outcomes include: airing the season later in the year moving it to a different platform, such as Hulu or reworking the release entirely While ABC has pulled The Bachelorette from its Sunday lineup, the situation is still evolving—and the season could still eventually see the light of day in some form. 🌹 SIGN UP for our The Bachelor newsletter to stay up to date on the latest Bachelor Nation news, exclusive interviews, episode recaps & more 🌹 If you or someone you know has been a victim of domestic violence, help is available 24 hours a day through the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-799-7233.
